options.text: The incident ray, the dashed normal, and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane.
A flat sheet under the rays can hold all three lines because they share one plane.
The dashed line is only another name for the incident ray, so only two lines matter.
The same-plane rule applies only to curved mirrors, not to this plane mirror.

stem:
The diagram shows Ojas's plane-mirror set-up. An incident ray meets the mirror at point O. The dashed line at O is drawn at 90° to the mirror. The reflected ray leaves O. Ojas keeps a flat cardboard sheet under these rays so he can trace them.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

teacher.key_rationale: The incident ray, the normal, and the reflected ray lie in one plane, so a flat sheet can hold all three. The normal is not the incident ray, and the rule is not limited to curved mirrors.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source lens ray figure into a plane-mirror reflection with incident ray, normal, reflected ray on a flat sheet.
